answer.stillOpen: No numerical half-life, decay constant, chapter-size limit or per-strength timer is approved. Deterministic grouping and retrieval from existing records can proceed; any consequential tuning is a separate proposal. The answer does not authorise false-memory generation or distortion.
answer.summary: Answered as a four-tier presentation and retrieval contract rather than a decay score. Landmark or self-defining memories stay available without a narrow cue: major relationship and family events, moves, education, job and office transitions, major successes and failures, severe crises, and events still tied to a durable goal or relationship. Accessible episodes need not stay on the top-level list but return when the current person, place, organisation, topic, role, goal or related event legitimately cues them. Chapter or gist compresses related routine episodes into a derived period summary with every underlying event still anchored, and chapter boundaries come from actual transitions — moves, role, relationship and household starts and ends, campaigns, terms, major family, health or world events — not arbitrary decades. Dormant traces are not listed and not treated as on the person's mind, but stay in append-only evidence and return under a strong cue, so 'gone' in ordinary play means not surfaced, never erased from the save. Accessibility uses represented facts (existing strength, recency, cue match, actual consequence, chapter-boundary status, meaningful later use) rather than a fake-precision universal decay number, and reopening the Journal, hovering, searching or Save/Continue is explicitly NOT rehearsal and may not refresh strength or age. It also corrected the question's premise from live source: MemoryRecord already carries faint/moderate/strong/defining strength, relevanceTags and supersedesMemoryId, and world39-journal already suppresses superseded memories, so this is extending existing seams upward, not a second memory engine.

notes: Nothing may be deleted. The history store is append-only on purpose and the save has to keep its evidence, so the answer is about what surfaces and how strongly, not about erasing rows.
Distortion is a separate question and is not being asked here. This is about what is recalled, not about whether the recollection is accurate.
question: Across a played lifetime of decades, which moments should a person still be able to recall unprompted, which should survive only as a general impression of a period or a person, and which should be gone entirely — and what makes the difference between the three?

title: How a person's memory of sixty years should compress without emptying
usableAnswer: A rule for what raises a moment above the rest and what lets one fade, expressed in terms the game can observe — how recent it was, how strongly it was felt, how often it has been revisited, who else was there, whether it changed the course of a life. Plus what a faded memory should leave behind, since an impression of a decade is not the same as nothing.
whyItMatters: Memories are appended and never pruned, superseded or weighted by age, so a sixty-year life ends with tens of thousands of equally live recollections and the journal and life record read as an undifferentiated log. The player's own sense of having lived a life depends on this more than on any other system, and the four strength levels the records already carry are set once at writing and never revisited.
